messages:
elyse: quick heads-up — nightly perf showed a regression on 4k sequences when the new kernel pipeline (pipeline-2) + fused-attn are enabled. not sure if it's scheduling or a stray memcpy. can someone try to reproduce on a dedicated card?

sachin: copying. do you have the nightly run id and the exact commit?

elyse: run id = nightly-2026-03-16-04, commit = refs/heads/attn/pipeline-2 @ 4b7c9d. cfg below:
```
model: gptx-7b
seq_len: 4096
batch: 4
kernels: [fused_attn, qkv_fuse, kv_prefetch:true]
quant: int8
prefill: true
```

taylor: can you also paste the raw p99 numbers from the dashboard? we should rule out noise.

elyse: p50 = 120ms, p95 = 260ms, p99 = 460ms (baseline w/o pipeline-2: p99 ~ 370ms). CPU steal was low.

benchbot: queued a reproduce job on dedicated-gpu-3 (job id: bb-8972). will post logs when done. :worker: 

sachin: I'll run a local debug build with NVTX enabled and an env that disables kv prefetch first. command I'll run: 
```bash
export ENABLE_NVTX=1
export KV_PREFETCH=0
./run_bench --model gptx-7b --seq 4096 --batch 4 --kernels fused_attn --runs 20
```

taylor: fyi the PR that changed scheduling also touched the op fusion pass — could be a backend ordering issue when prefill is true. worth checking trace ordering around `attn_forward` vs `kv_write`.

benchbot: reproduce job finished: local p99=472ms, saw a burst at step 2-3 where memcpy(Host->Device) spikes. attaching tail of the log:
```
[bb-8972] step 2 memcpy 18.6ms (host->device)
[bb-8972] step 3 memcpy 20.1ms (host->device)
[bb-8972] attn_forward 6.2ms
[bb-8972] kv_write 12.0ms
```

elyse: interesting — memcpy spikes only when prefill=true and quant=int8. maybe a pinned-memory fallback is happening because of the quantized buffer size pattern.

sachin: running with quant disabled now (int32) to see if pattern goes away. also will try building with the older allocator path (alloc-v1) to compare.

ci-bot: smoke-test triggered for PR #4128 (attn/pipeline-2). status: running. :gear:

sachin: quick numbers with quant off: p99=378ms, memcpy spikes absent. so quant path likely triggers fallback.

taylor: can you dump the allocator stats from the run? `ALLOC_STATS=1 ./run_bench ...` should show whether we hit host staging buffers.

sachin: yep will paste after next run. planning to add a small patch to avoid falling back to staging for sizes that match our tensor patterns. if that helps, we can put a guard in the pipeline scheduler too.

elyse: thanks all. next steps: (1) sachin to confirm allocator trace and post patch; (2) taylor to review PR for scheduler guard; (3) benchbot to run canary with the patch on the nightly matrix. I'll update the ticket with run ids. :thumbsup:

benchbot: canary queued bb-8980 (with sachin's upcoming patch) — will report back.

sachin: posted allocator trace and a tiny patch in draft PR #4132. comments welcome, I added unit tests for the allocation path.

taylor: taking a look now, will leave inline comments. if it looks good I'll merge to a canary branch and ask benchbot to run the end-to-end matrix.

elyse: perfect. if we see >5% regression at p95 or p99 after the patch we should revert pipeline-2 in nightly until we get a fix.

sachin: agreed. I'll ping here once bb-8980 completes.

benchbot: bb-8980 done: p99 = 375ms (down from 472ms), memcpy spikes gone. marking canary as pass. :white_check_mark:

elyse: incredible — great triage everyone. we'll keep monitoring but closing the immediate regression loop.

taylor: nice work. will follow up with a small perf regression card to track long-tail cases.

sachin: thanks. I'll merge the allocator fix and follow up with a postmortem note on the ticket.

ci-bot: PR #4132 merged to canary branch. deployments scheduled.
